steps.body: Sometimes the pairing comes out even: every star finds a heart, and nothing stands alone. Those groups MATCH — they are EQUAL.
steps.narration: Sometimes the pairing comes out even: every star finds a heart, and nothing stands alone. Those groups MATCH — they are EQUAL.

widget.prompt: 6 hearts wait. Build the star group that matches EXACTLY.

commonCounts.feedback: Five stars leave one heart alone; a single gap breaks the match.
Seven stars leave one star alone; one extra breaks the match just as surely.

widget.missFeedback: One star per heart, no more, no fewer.
widget.successFeedback: Six for six — every star paired, every heart paired, nothing left on either side.

predict.prompt: Groups match exactly. Now the stars are scattered about. Still equal?

options.label: Yes — pairing does not care about position

predict.reveal: Equal is about the pairing, and every scattered star still finds its heart.

cml.actionGoal: Pair the groups one to one, or place both numbers in the counting song, for kcm equal groups.
invariants: Comparison rests on two facts that never move: pairing one to one leaves the bigger group with leftovers, and a number later in the counting song always names more — which is what kcm equal groups uses.
misconceptions: Judging by how much space a group fills, by the size of the things in it, or by which number was written first.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more joined the smaller group, would the pairing come out even?

widget.prompt: There are 4 stars and 4 hearts. Which statement is true?

options.label: They are equal
options.feedback: Correct — every star pairs with exactly one heart and neither side has anything left over.

options.label: More hearts
options.feedback: Pairing one to one uses every heart with stars to spare, so the hearts are not the larger group.

options.label: You cannot tell
options.feedback: You can always tell — pair the groups one to one and look at which side has leftovers.

widget.prompt: Start at 11 and count on 2. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 12 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 13.
14 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 2 hops from 11 to land on 13.

widget.missFeedback: Count 2 on from 11: you land on 13.
widget.successFeedback: 11 and 2 more is 13 — every step forward lands on a greater number.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 2 counts are needed to reach 13.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 2 numbers, on 13.
